messages:
alex_sales: Heads-up — large EU customer (FinRegCo) asking that no customer content leave EU boundaries, including fallthrough failovers. Can we confirm our default routing and what we can contractually guarantee? Need answers for Monday. @maria_se @pri_sec

maria_se: Short answer: hosted API has region_preference by default and may fall back cross-region. We can provide tenant pinning to EU for stronger guarantees, and Dedicated/Private for contractual guarantees. Sending links. :link:

sam_prod: Details — our routing modes: `region_preference` (prefer EU, fallthrough allowed), `strict_geofence` (no cross-region egress; rejects if no capacity). For strict guarantees we require Dedicated capacity or Private. Example config:```yaml
route_policy: strict_geofence
pin_region: eu-west-1
fallback: none
```

pri_sec: Security/legal notes: we can include subprocessors list + DPA clauses restricting processing to EU. Caveats: backups, aggregated metrics, and some monitoring pipelines default to central infra — those must be scoped out or moved under EU-only processing. KMS key residency required for full guarantee.

oliver_legal: To commit contractually we need an audited subprocessor list (cloud infra, logging vendor, CDN). I can approve redlines if Eng confirms that no telemetry/replication leaves EU when `strict_geofence` is enabled.

ryan_sre: Ops perspective: we have a runbook for regional failover. If `strict_geofence` is enabled and local capacity is exhausted we return 503s rather than failing over to another region. Alternative: if customer agrees, we can route to a customer-managed on-prem gateway via private peering. Runbook excerpt:
```
1) monitor regional queue depth (SLO: <60s queue)
2) auto-scale dedicated pool (if autoscale enabled)
3) if threshold breached and no capacity: return 503 + alert to oncall
4) if private peering configured: failover to customer gateway per contract
```

alex_sales: Customer says rejects are not ideal — they'd prefer automatic peering failover to an on-prem gateway we manage. Realistic?

sam_prod: We can support that but only with Private deployment or Dedicated with VPC peering. Hosted customers cannot get guaranteed private peering. Technical work: set up VPC/VPN, route tables, and NAT rules. Also need an SLA-add on for the peering route.

maria_se: Pricing note: strict_geofence + reserved capacity adds ~40% to committed monthly price vs standard hosted. Private + peering is higher (setup fee + monthly infra). I'll draft a quick estimate. :moneybag:

jordan_ps: For the POC we can propose: 2-week EU Dedicated pool with relaxed logging retention + scoped DPA. That proves behaviour and then convert to Dedicated long-term.

alex_sales: Can someone drop a short bulleted summary I can paste into the customer's SOC/security questionnaire? Need: subprocessors list (current), routing guarantees, fallback behaviour, KMS residency options, and cost delta.

pri_sec: I'll draft DPA language + subprocessors list. Quick note: currently metrics ingestion touches a US telemetry collector unless we toggle EU-only metrics — pinging infra.

infra_bot: deploy-bot: infra alert — eu-west-1 capacity at 78% — scale job queued.

ryan_sre: Noted. ETA for scale job ~15m. Will update ops channel when complete.

oliver_legal: I'll prepare DPA/redline by EOD, need final runbook + list of services in scope to attach.

alex_sales: Great — summary for customer I will send now: 1) Hosted: region_preference, may fall back cross-region (no guarantee). 2) Strict geofence: avoid cross-region egress but requires Dedicated/Private; on overflow requests are rejected (503) unless explicit peering failover is contracted. 3) We can provide DPA + subprocessors list; KMS residency and metrics retention must be scoped in contract. 4) Pricing: ~+40% for reserved strict-geofence; Private+peering priced separately. Will follow up with numbers and redlines. Thanks all. :pray:
